tin noun

classical

Caes. BG 5.12 (Lewis & Short s.v. plumbum)
Lucr. 6.1079 (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 395

plumbum album

tin (“white lead”)

Classical Latin calls tin “white lead”, and lead itself plumbum nigrum or plain plumbum; Pliny also says plumbum candidum.

Other words

  • stannum, stannī n. — tin

    noun, second declension · also used · late Latin · Isid. Orig. 16.22 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 395 · Declension on Wiktionary

    In Pliny and Suetonius stannum is an alloy of silver and lead; Lewis & Short gives the sense “tin” as late Latin (Jerome, Isidore).

See also tin, sheet metal.
